routes.label: Track the cubes of the terms

question: Define a sequence of real numbers \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\ldots\) by \(a_1 = 1\) and \(a_{n+1}^3 = 99 a_n^3\) for all \(n \ge 1.\) Then \(a_{100}\) equals
solution:
The recurrence gives a simple multiplication rule for the cubes. Define \(b_n=a_n^3\) for \(n\ge1\). Then
\[
b_1=1,\qquad b_{n+1}=99b_n.
\]
Each step introduces one factor of \(99\). Reaching term \(n\) from term \(1\) takes \(n-1\) steps, so \(b_n=99^{n-1}\). In particular,
\[
a_{100}^3=b_{100}=99^{99}=(99^{33})^3.
\]
Every real number has a unique real cube root, so \(a_{100}=99^{33}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
